Mark Range read methods and Selection#containsNode() [Affects=Nothing]

DevTools Console eager evaluation and the DevTools AI executeJavaScript
tool evaluate expressions with throwOnSideEffect: true. Read-only Range
geometry and boundary comparisons and Selection#containsNode() abort
with EvalError because they lack [Affects=Nothing].

Blink's IDL compiler defaults methods to [Affects=Everything] unless
annotated. Each annotated operation flushes style or layout where
required or compares existing DOM endpoints without firing events or
mutating DOM or selection state.

- Add [Affects=Nothing] to Range#cloneRange(), compareBoundaryPoints(),
  isPointInRange(), comparePoint(), intersectsNode(), getClientRects(),
  and getBoundingClientRect().
- Add [Affects=Nothing] to Selection#containsNode(), leaving
  getRangeAt() and getComposedRanges() unannotated because materializing
  cached_range_ changes subsequent rangeCount checks.

[pip-ext] 25. Add end-to-end Document PiP extension API parity tests

Add parameterized DocumentPipExtensionApiParityBrowserTest coverage
comparing legacy browser-backed and standalone Document
Picture-in-Picture windows across:
- chrome.windows APIs and events (get, getAll, update, remove,
  onCreated, onBoundsChanged, and onRemoved)
- chrome.tabs APIs (get, getSelected, getAllInWindow, query, update,
  reload, discard, setZoom, getZoom, and remove)
- MV3 chrome.scripting.executeScript(), chrome.runtime.sendMessage()
  sender.tab metadata, and extension subframe calls to
  chrome.tabs.getCurrent(), chrome.windows.getCurrent(), and
  chrome.tabs.query({currentWindow: true})

Also exercise ExtensionTabUtil::OpenOptionsPageFromWebContents()
directly in OptionsPageOpensInNormalBrowser.

updater: remove json::Covers() and json::HasAppMatching()

After the request matching moved to json:: matchers, Covers() has one
caller, the request attributes in ExpectAppsUpdateSequence(), and
HasAppMatching() has none.

ExpectAppsUpdateSequence() now takes an optional matcher for the update
check's `request` dict instead of a dict for Covers(). The matcher comes
after `apps` and defaults to std::nullopt, so most callers omit it. The
two tests that check request attributes pass
json::HasKey("dlpref", "cacheable"), which, unlike Covers(), compares
the value case-sensitively and by type. Remove Covers(),
HasAppMatching(), and their tests, and move the "is empty" explanation
check for list entries to the HasEvent() test.

The ExpectAppsUpdateSequence() comment now uses the dotted names of the
`updatecheck` keys. The HasKey() comment says how to compare strings
case-insensitively, and the IsString() test covers it.

Ash: Move the video conference listener to MediaCaptureDispatcher

This CL is part of an ongoing series to remove Ash code's dependency
on MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher, a //chrome singleton, by moving Ash
callers to an interface in components/webrtc that the dispatcher
implements.

On devices with video conference controls in the shelf, when a website
starts or stops using the camera or microphone, or starts or stops
sharing a tab, window or screen, VideoConferenceMediaListener notices
and Ash updates those controls. This CL makes the listener observe
webrtc::MediaCaptureIndicator, which it gets from
webrtc::MediaCaptureDispatcher, instead of MediaStreamCaptureIndicator.
MediaStreamCaptureIndicator implements webrtc::MediaCaptureIndicator
and is the instance the dispatcher returns, so the listener receives
the same notifications as before. In
chrome/browser/ash/video_conference, production code no longer depends
on //chrome/browser/media/webrtc; only the browser tests still do.

Revert "[A11y] Route ariaOwnsElements and ElementInternals via hardened path"

This reverts commit 75344f8ac03dcda49e298878a9ba97828e9125ab.

Reason for revert: Culprit of virtual/force-renderer-accessibility/external/wpt/accessibility/crashtests/aria-owns-elements-deferred-parent-cycle.html (Linux Tests (dbg)(1), flaky)

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20Tests%20%28dbg%29%281%29/135063/overview

Original change's description:
> [A11y] Route ariaOwnsElements and ElementInternals via hardened path
>
> Until now, Element.ariaOwnsElements went through a separate, older code
> path in AXRelationCache than ID-based aria-owns, and
> ElementInternals.ariaOwnsElements was still a TODO (crbug.com/41469336).
>
> The element-reference path had missed several stability fixes that the
> ID path picked up over time—most notably, if GetOrCreate() failed on one
> candidate child, it returned early and left the ownership maps in a
> half-updated state.
>
> This change funnels IDs, Element.ariaOwnsElements, and
> ElementInternals.ariaOwnsElements through the same validated loop in
> AXRelationCache::UpdateAriaOwnsWithCleanLayout(), so element references
> get the same preemptive child-to-owner mapping, previous-owner check,
> and deduplication as IDs, and a skipped child no longer aborts the rest
> of the list.
> A few related pieces are wired up at the same time:
> - AXObject::HasARIAOwns() now checks ElementInternals so custom element
>   owners are included in the tree and queued for aria-owns updates.
> - MaybeRestoreParentOfOwnedChild() re-queues competing owners that
>   referenced the child via ariaOwnsElements, not just by ID.
> - Ownership is restricted to the owner's TreeScope. DOM element
>   references can legally point into ancestor shadow trees (and
>   ElementInternals references aren't scope-checked at all), so keeping
>   aria-owns within the same TreeScope avoids cross-shadow ownership and
>   matches ID-based aria-owns and Reference Target.
>
> There's no web-exposed change yet: ariaOwnsElements stays behind the
> existing AOMAriaRelationshipPropertiesAriaOwns flag while we harden it.
>
> Bug: 406816521, 341745130
>

Wayland: force damage on frames that ack a window state change

When the compositor sends an xdg_toplevel configure that changes only
the window state (e.g. maximizing a window that already fills the work
area with server-side decorations),
WindowTreeHostPlatform::OnStateUpdate() allocates a new LocalSurfaceId
and WaylandWindow waits for a frame with that id to be swapped before
sending xdg_surface.ack_configure and committing. If the relayout
doesn't damage any layer, cc submits the frame with an empty damage rect
and viz skips drawing and swapping it, so the configure is not acked
until an unrelated repaint happens. After three such configures,
MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS is reached and later configures (including real
resizes) are not applied at all.

Add LayerTreeHost::SetNeedsCommitWithMinimalDamage(), which makes the
next activation add a 1x1 viewport damage rect, and use it from
OnStateUpdate() whenever a LocalSurfaceId is allocated. This guarantees
a swap carrying the sequence id while keeping the extra work minimal.
Unlike SetNeedsCommitWithForcedRedraw(), it doesn't stop deferring
commits.

[chromium-bidi] Send only ACL-allowed events in restricted sessions

- In restricted sessions (`"goog:sessionType": "restricted"`), send an
  event only if the ACL lists it in `events`, session-wide in `default`
  or for the event's tab in `perNavigable`. Events without a tab need a
  `default` grant. An ACL can list `browsingContext.contextCreated`,
  `browsingContext.contextDestroyed`, `browsingContext.fragmentNavigated`,
  `browsingContext.historyUpdated`, `browsingContext.navigationCommitted`,
  `browsingContext.userPromptClosed`, `browsingContext.userPromptOpened`
  and `log.entryAdded`; other events grant nothing. Like `commands`, the
  returned ACL always has `events`.
- Events can leak data from the user's other tabs, e.g. URLs, console
  messages or dialog text, so the ACL controls them like commands, as
  in https://github.com/WICG/agentic-webdriver-bidi.
- `session.subscribe` and `session.unsubscribe` work without an ACL
  grant and accept any event or module. Instead of subscribing to the
  events in the ACL (the proposal's open question 6), check each event
  when it is sent, so `goog:session.setAcl` changes apply to existing
  subscriptions. Events withheld from a channel are not replayed after
  a later grant. Unrestricted sessions are unchanged.

Translator API: record CreateTranslatorError on create() failure

Record Translate.TranslatorApi.CreateTranslatorError when a
Translator.create() call reaching the service controller fails while the
renderer client remains connected, using the CreateTranslatorError value
sent to the renderer. Track in-flight clients in a mojo::RemoteSet so
aborted or disconnected requests are skipped.

[Public Transit] Replace closeCurrentTab() in tests without a usable Station

Migrate the remaining callers of ChromeTabUtils#closeCurrentTab() and
delete it. Add a Station-less Trigger,
ChromeTriggers#closeCurrentTabTo(ChromeTabbedActivity). The callers wait
for the TabClosingCondition, which closeCurrentTab() also waited for.

TabsTest#testCloseTabDuringFling gets a Station and uses
closeCurrentTabFast() instead.

Add UseCounter for mixed-content requests in SharedWorkers

Add WebFeature::kMixedContentInSharedWorker and record it in
MixedContentChecker::ShouldBlockFetchOnWorker and
MixedContentChecker::IsWebSocketAllowed when a SharedWorkerGlobalScope
initiates a mixed-content request.

This measures how frequently HTTPS SharedWorkers issue insecure
subresource or WebSocket requests before rolling out mixed-content
blocking.

Ash: Move the media client to MediaCaptureDispatcher

This CL is part of an ongoing series to remove Ash code's dependency
on MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher, a //chrome singleton, by moving Ash
callers to an interface in components/webrtc that the dispatcher
implements.

When a web page, app or extension starts or stops using the camera or
microphone, Ash's media client updates the capture state that Ash shows
next to the user's name in the Quick Settings user list. This CL makes
MediaClientImpl use webrtc::MediaCaptureDispatcher to learn about media
requests and webrtc::MediaCaptureIndicator to check which WebContents
are capturing, so the media client no longer depends on
//chrome/browser/media/webrtc. That target still lists
//chrome/browser/ui/ash/media_client in its deps and
allow_circular_includes_from; a follow-up CL removes both entries.

Ash: Move Shimless RMA media access to MediaCaptureDispatcher

This CL is part of an ongoing series to remove Ash code's dependency
on MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher, a //chrome singleton, by moving Ash
callers to an interface in components/webrtc that the dispatcher
implements.

During Shimless RMA, when a third-party diagnostics app asks to use the
camera or microphone, ExternalAppDialog forwards the request through
ChromeShimlessRmaDelegate. This CL makes ChromeShimlessRmaDelegate use
webrtc::MediaCaptureDispatcher instead of MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher,
so chrome/browser/ash/shimless_rma no longer depends on
//chrome/browser/media/webrtc. ExternalAppDialog is the only caller of
ShimlessRmaDelegate::ProcessMediaAccessRequest and always passes a null
extension, so ChromeShimlessRmaDelegate checks that the extension is
null before forwarding; removing the unused parameter from
ShimlessRmaDelegate is left to a follow-up CL.

[Nearby Share] Fix data race on BleV2RemotePeripheral::GetAddress

Cache the immutable Bluetooth address in BleV2RemotePeripheral at
construction and remove the unused device_info_ member so GetAddress()
cannot race with concurrent UpdateDeviceInfo() calls on the
AdapterObserver sequence. Additionally, guard
BleV2Medium::discovered_ble_peripherals_map_ with a base::Lock across
StartScanning(), ConnectToGattServer(), DeviceAdded(), and Shutdown().

Reland "Linux: Show unshown browser windows on BaseWindow::Activate()"

This is a reland of commit fac6ac975ad141a04c9474c5966a63548e83a257.

The original change made Activate() show a browser window that was
never shown, which exposed a DCHECK_EQ in LoadRestoredTabIfVisible()
during session and tab restore when the NTP footer is visible: the
synchronous layout shrinks the WebContents by the footer height while
BrowserView::GetContentsSize() returns the size of the whole contents
container. This reland drops that DCHECK_EQ (the WebContents can be
smaller than the container) and adds FooterControllerRestoreTest,
which crashed on the DCHECK before this change.

Original change's description:
> Linux: Show unshown browser windows on BaseWindow::Activate()
>
> BrowserView::Activate() on a browser window that was never shown
> (e.g. one returned by CreateBrowserWindow()) reported the browser as
> active via BrowserActiveStateManager, but X11Window::Activate()
> ignores activation requests for unmapped windows. The window stayed
> hidden and the previously active window was never deactivated. On
> Mac, activating a hidden window shows it, so the behavior differed.
>
> On Linux, delegate to Show() when the widget is not visible. Show()
> already handles the visible case by calling Activate(), so the two
> are now symmetric.
>
> Enable GlobalBrowserCollectionTest on Linux. Wayland compositors
> refuse to activate an already-mapped window without an activation
> token from user input, so the tests stay filtered out on the Weston
> and Mutter bots.
>
> Fixed: 483363917
> Change-Id: Ib953b17dfe1eb57bb2f9d326855f1cd1747cc331
> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8760984

69b97e67fc272993cfd2f4e4be31ba6ade962a12 [ diff ] 
[search] Wait for typed suggestions before acting in Tab Search tests

TabSearchOverlayFacility#typeInSearchBox returned as soon as any
suggestions were shown, which the zero-prefix list already satisfies.
If "One" happened to be row 0 of that list, the Enter test pressed Enter
before the typed autocomplete request had started; loadTypedOmniboxText
then cancelled it and, since the URL bar text did not match the last
received results, did nothing. The overlay stayed open and the batch
cascaded.

Add SuggestionsReceivedForTextCondition, backed by a ForTesting getter
for the text the latest suggestions were received for (the same check
Enter performs), and wait on it after typing. Re-enable the test and
hide any leftover overlay in @After so one failure cannot cascade.

android: Filter gtests, adjust shards, and set slow-start for Canary

Green and stabilize suites on android-canary-x64-fyi-rel:

- Reuse existing emulator test filters already applied on
  android-16-x64-rel / android-17-x64-rel (https://crrev.com/c/8682611)
  for base_unittests, content_unittests, gl_tests_validating,
  gwp_asan_unittests, media_unittests, and perfetto_unittests.
- Increase shards on android-canary-x64-fyi-rel (android_browsertests:
  6 -> 10, android_browsertests_no_fieldtrial: 6 -> 10,
  chrome_public_test_apk: 20 -> 30, content_browsertests: 15 -> 30),
  reducing 40-45 minute max shard runtimes and batch timeouts.
- Include 'canary' in avd.py slow-start emulator types alongside '36'
  and '37' (https://crrev.com/c/8817078) so WaitUntilFullyBooted uses
  the 360s timeout instead of 90s.

[🌱][Android] Re-enable video tests on Android 17

These 34 tests (all of the content_browsertests Android 17 filter,
MediaCodecBridgeTest.PresentationTimestampsDoNotDecrease and
ThumbnailMediaParserTest#testParseVideoThumbnailH265) were disabled
because video decode failed on the Android 17 emulator. The root cause
was a sepolicy change missing from the android-37.0 system images,
which kept apps from talking to the codec2 HAL. The Android 17 AVDs
moved to android-37.2 (crrev.com/c/8716551), which includes that
change, so the tests should pass again.

[NavigationPredictor] Re-enable user interaction test on non-Android

Re-enables the user interaction metrics test for invalid UKM source IDs
on non-Android platforms.

The test was disabled universally in https://crrev.com/c/4500323 using
`DISABLED_UserInteractionMetricsIgnoresUpdatesForInvalidUkmSourceId` due
to flakiness on Android (https://crbug.com/40266872). The test uses
`EXPECT_DEATH` to verify that `RecordUserInteractionMetrics` crashes
when the UKM source ID is mismatched. Disabling it universally
inadvertently removed coverage on desktop platforms where the test runs
reliably.

Guards the test definition with `BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)` using
`MAYBE_UserInteractionMetricsIgnoresUpdatesForInvalidUkmSourceId` so it
remains disabled on Android while executing on non-Android platforms.
Also adds documentation comments detailing the scenario, preconditions,
and expectations for the test.

Verified on macOS and Linux.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Reland "[3p freshness] apr: Update to 1.7.6"

This is a reland of commit dd567fd328a99dff9312c80b49dab902922a5ac8

The original was reverted because it broke android-cronet-x86-dbg:
atomic/unix/builtins64.c fails with -Watomic-alignment on 32-bit x86,
where 64-bit integers are only 4-byte aligned, so the 64-bit atomic
builtins on apr_uint64_t are misaligned.

Fix: apply_android_edits.py now guards HAVE_ATOMIC_BUILTINS64 and
HAVE__ATOMIC_BUILTINS64 with !defined(__i386__), so 32-bit x86 uses
APR's mutex-based 64-bit atomics (atomic/unix/mutex64.c, already built)
and the other architectures keep the builtins. apr_private.h is
regenerated accordingly. Also sort a BUILD.gn sources list (gn format).

Tested: //third_party/apache-portable-runtime:apr and
//third_party/netty-tcnative:netty-tcnative-so for Cronet Android x86
(debug), arm, arm64 and x64. The x86 build reproduced the error without
the fix.

Original change's description:
> [3p freshness] apr: Update to 1.7.6
>
> Roll third_party/apache-portable-runtime/src from 1.5.2 (2015) to 1.7.6
> (2025-05-16), the latest release.
>
> Regenerate include/apr.h and include/arch/unix/apr_private.h: run
> ./configure from the 1.7.6 release tarball on Linux, as for 1.5.2, then
> apply the Android edits with the new apply_android_edits.py. The script
> applies the edits that diff.patch used to carry, plus a few for code and
> checks that are new since 1.5.2:
> - HAVE_DECL_SYS_SIGLIST: bionic declares sys_siglist, newer glibc does
>   not, so configure on Linux no longer detects it.
> - getrandom() needs API level 28 (Cronet's minimum is 24), so keep
>   reading /dev/urandom as before.
> - No shm_open() in bionic and no SysV semaphores (semtimedop() needs API
>   level 26).
>
> 1.5.2's change of apr_int64_t from long to long long is no longer needed:
> apr.h now uses int64_t.
>
> BUILD.gn: add the new Unix sources for 64-bit atomics and pollset
> wakeup. Like encoding/apr_escape.c before, the new optional APIs
> (apr_encode, apr_cstr) are not built because nothing uses them.
>
> include/DEPS: apr_private.h now includes "arch/apr_private_common.h"
> (found through src/include), which checkdeps needs to allow.
>
> README.chromium: version, and how to regenerate the headers.
>
> Built //third_party/netty-tcnative:netty-tcnative-so for Cronet Android
> arm and arm64 (min SDK 24). The only new libc symbol it needs is
> if_indextoname(), available at all API levels.

[pip-ext] 24. Support standalone windows in TabsGetSelected and TabUtil

Complete standalone WindowController support across three remaining
chrome.tabs and ExtensionTabUtil helpers:
1. In TabsGetSelectedFunction::Run(), check
   ExtensionTabUtil::IsTabStripEditable() and resolve the active
   WebContents via WindowController::GetActiveTab() instead of requiring
   a BrowserWindowInterface.
2. In ExtensionTabUtil::CreateTabObject(), resolve tab_index from
   GetWindowControllerOfTab() when tab_list is null and tab_index is -1
   so 3-argument callers (such as TabsGetCurrentFunction) report index 0
   instead of -1 for standalone windows.
3. In ExtensionTabUtil::OpenOptionsPageFromWebContents(), delegate to
   GetWindowControllerOfTab()->OpenOptionsPage() instead of requiring
   GetBrowserForTabContents().

[ServiceWorker] Persist synthetic response headers in database

Currently, response headers captured for ServiceWorker synthetic
responses are held only in memory on `ServiceWorkerVersion`, so browser
restarts or version teardown require a cold navigation before a
synthetic response can be served again.

This CL adds LevelDB persistence for synthetic response headers in
`ServiceWorkerDatabase` under the `SYNTHETIC_RESPONSE_HEADER:` prefix,
keyed by serialized first-party `blink::StorageKey` independently of
registration records:

- Extract `ConvertPickleToURLResponseHead()` and
  `ConvertURLResponseHeadToPickle()` in `service_worker_resource_ops`
  so `ServiceWorkerDatabase` shares `net::HttpResponseInfo` pickle
  serialization with disk-cache resource readers/writers.
- `WriteSyntheticResponseEntry()` serializes the format version,
  capture timestamp, scope URL, `FetchResponseType`,
  `timing_allow_passed`, and `HttpResponseInfo` pickle (with
  `skip_transient_headers=false`, stripping cookie headers via
  `HttpResponseHeaders::PERSIST_SANS_COOKIES` while retaining
  hop-by-hop and security-state headers for consistency checks). It
  caps total stored entries at `kMaxSyntheticResponseEntries` (32) by
  evicting the oldest entries in the same `WriteBatch`.
- `ReadSyntheticResponseEntry()` returns the stored `URLResponseHead`
  if its version, scope, and `max_age` match, or deletes the entry and
  returns `kErrorNotFound` otherwise.
- `GetSyntheticResponseStorageKeys()`,
  `DeleteSyntheticResponseEntries()`, and `DeleteAllDataForOrigins()`
  list and purge stored entries by key or origin.

[WebUI] Cache generated colors.css stylesheets in ThemeSource

ThemeSource::GenerateColorsCss() generates the stylesheet from scratch
for every request. However, many requests are for a stylesheet that was
just generated: the WebUI pages of a window mostly request the same
stylesheet for the same ColorProvider when they load, again as soon as
their ColorChangeUpdater is started (ColorChangeHandler::SetPage()
triggers a refresh), and again after every theme change.

Cache recently generated stylesheets in a small LRU cache of size 8. The
cache is keyed by the unique id of the ColorProvider and by the request
parameters. Keying by the id relies on a ColorProvider not being
modified once it is in use, see ColorProvider::unique_id(). To ensure
that the key covers everything the request contributes to the
stylesheet, the request URL is now parsed into a ColorsCssParams struct
up front and the generator is only passed these parameters instead of
the URL.

The cache is behind the new feature ColorIdCssStyleSheetCache, which is
disabled by default and enabled in the field trial testing config. With
eight "ui,chrome" stylesheets cached it retains about 0.7 MB (8 x
82.5 KB).

The cache key does not include the state of
ColorIdCssStyleSheetOptimization, which selects the generator
implementation and does not change while the browser is running. Unit
tests that toggle that feature for a single ColorProvider rely on the
cache being disabled by default to exercise both implementations.

Measured with a microbenchmark in unit_tests (release build, Linux) for
the "ui,chrome" stylesheet with ColorIdCssStyleSheetOptimization,
ThemeChangeOptimization and ThemeChangeOptimizationV2 enabled:
- Repeated request for a ColorProvider: 208 us -> 5 us, or 298 us ->
  54 us if the allocator reclaimed its free memory between requests.
- First request for a ColorProvider: 1393 us -> 1454 us (+4%), or
  1414 us -> 1489 us (+5%) after a reclaim. This includes copying the
  stylesheet into the cache.
In a sample of 39 browser tests, 147 of 206 colors.css requests were

a856a3e46854f60b7bb321d863aff39556eec639 [ diff ] 
Honor IPv6 probe for platform DNS with empty config

During host resolution, local IPv6 configuration was only read when
nameservers or DoH servers were populated, assuming local IPv6 might
be needed otherwise so system resolution (such as DirectAccess or
split-DNS VPNs) is not restricted to IPv4 without a valid DNS
configuration.

However, platform DNS can run insecure DNS transactions before the
system DNS configuration is populated, which caused cold-start lookups
on IPv4-only networks to still send AAAA queries.

Also read the effective DNS configuration's local IPv6 setting
whenever insecure or secure DNS transactions are usable.

[ServiceWorker] Do not re-intercept raced subresource network redirects

When `race-network-and-fetch-handler` is used for a subresource request
and the fetch handler falls back (causing `OnFallback()` to set commit
responsibility to `FetchResponseFrom::kWithoutServiceWorker`) before a
redirect response arrives from the raced network request,
`ServiceWorkerRaceNetworkRequestURLLoaderClient::OnReceiveRedirect()`
previously forwarded the redirect to
`ServiceWorkerSubresourceLoader::HandleRedirect()`. When the client
followed the redirect, `FollowRedirect()` reset commit responsibility
and dispatched a new `FetchEvent` to the service worker for the
redirect target URL.

Per the Fetch specification (HTTP fetch, Step 4.2), once a service
worker declines to respond and the request falls back to the network,
subsequent redirects in the redirect chain must be followed by the
network without re-entering the service worker. Re-dispatching a
`FetchEvent` on a redirect hop after fallback exposes post-redirect
cross-origin URLs (including credentialed redirect parameters) to the
service worker via `event.request.url`.

Starting a fresh network request from `FollowRedirect()` at the
redirect target URL would also bypass the original `CorsURLLoader`
state machine (`tainted_`, `fetch_cors_flag_`, and `redirect_count_`),
causing cross-origin redirects back to a same-origin URL in `no-cors`
mode to lose their opaque response tainting.

This change fixes subresource redirects under `kWithoutServiceWorker`
in two ways:
1. When the raced network `URLLoader` has not been consumed by a
   `fetch(event.request)` call inside the service worker,
   `ServiceWorkerSubresourceLoader` reclaims the in-flight `URLLoader`
   via `TakeURLLoader()` and forwards `FollowRedirect()` directly on
   that pipe, preserving the active `CorsURLLoader` state across hops
   and committing the final response via `kForwardToOwner`.
2. When the raced network `URLLoader` was already fused to the service
   worker's `fetch(event.request)` call,
   `ServiceWorkerSubresourceLoader` hands the page's request to
   `fallback_factory_` while keeping itself alive until forwarding to
   the service worker completes.

Use UserSessionTestEnvironment in CupsPrintJobNotificationTest

CupsPrintJobNotificationTest set up the user and the Profile manually
with FakeChromeUserManager and a standalone TestingProfile, and
annotated AccountId after the Profile was created.

This CL migrates the test to UserSessionTestEnvironment with
ChromeUserSessionTestEnvironmentDelegate, so that the user session and
the Profile are set up in the same way as production, e.g., AccountId
is annotated on Profile creation, and the User's profile prefs are set
via ProfileUserManagerController.

Revert "[A11y] Deflake AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName dump test"

This reverts commit 5394d1b891d4bd9dfd2a3336955d0a0d2a8b2319.

Reason for revert:
LUCI Bisection has identified this change as the cause of a test failure. See the analysis: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/test-analysis/b/6083979800215552

Sample build with failed test: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8664644830377969313
Affected test(s):
[://content/test\:content_browsertests!gtest::DumpAccessibilityTreeTest#AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName/All.blink](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fcontent%2Ftest%5C:content_browsertests%21gtest::DumpAccessibilityTreeTest%23AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName%2FAll.blink?q=VHash%3Ab74e387ec6ddcb7a)
[://content/test\:content_browsertests!gtest::DumpAccessibilityTreeTest#AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName/All.linux](https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/:%2F%2Fcontent%2Ftest%5C:content_browsertests%21gtest::DumpAccessibilityTreeTest%23AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName%2FAll.linux?q=VHash%3Ab74e387ec6ddcb7a)

If this is a false positive, please report it at http://b.corp.google.com/createIssue?component=1199205&description=Analysis%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fci.chromium.org%2Fui%2Fp%2Fchromium%2Fbisection%2Ftest-analysis%2Fb%2F6083979800215552&format=PLAIN&priority=P3&title=Wrongly+blamed+https%3A%2F%2Fchromium-review.googlesource.com%2Fc%2Fchromium%2Fsrc%2F%2B%2F8836684&type=BUG

Original change's description:
> [A11y] Deflake AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName dump test
>
> DumpAccessibilityTreeTest.AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName/linux
> failed 1 of 20 repeats in the new-test flakiness check on
> linux_chromium_asan_rel_ng. In the failing run the dumped tree was
> missing one of the whitespace static text nodes between the inline
> <video> elements; every other line matched the expectation.
>
> The test covers the accessible names of the media elements, not the
> whitespace between them. Make the elements in the test page
> block-level so that the whitespace between them generates no nodes,
> and drop those nodes from the expectation files.
>

[tips] Count opt-in promo shows when the sheet opens and skip decliners

- Record Shown, the show count and the last-shown timestamp when the
  Tips sheet first opens, not when it's requested. A request dropped
  before opening (e.g. by tab restore on cold start) no longer uses up
  one of the user's two shows.
- Only react to the Tips sheet in the sheet observer, so other sheets
  can't log a false Ignored or remove it.
- Add a Closed by system value to
  Notifications.Tips.OptInPromo.EventType2 for closes without a user
  choice, so each show records exactly one outcome. A sheet hidden
  temporarily (e.g. while the omnibox is focused) records its outcome
  once it's destroyed, since it can open again.
- Skip the promo once tips_v2 exists. Declining creates it as blocked,
  but users who declined still got a second show. This also covers
  users who declined before this change; they can still turn Tips on
  in system settings.
- Skip users with Chrome notifications off, since accepting would only
  send them to system settings.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[Notifications.Tips.OptInPromo.EventType2]=Replaced by
Notifications.Tips.OptInPromo.EventType3 in M160; Shown is now recorded
when the sheet opens rather than when requested, and system closes are
recorded.

[blink] Store byte stream autoAllocateChunkSize as uint64_t

Store ReadableByteStreamController::auto_allocate_chunk_size_ as
uint64_t instead of casting UnderlyingSource.autoAllocateChunkSize
([EnforceRange] unsigned long long) to size_t during setup, and check
base::IsValueInRangeForNumericType<size_t>() before allocating in
PullSteps().

Previously on 32-bit platforms, values such as 2^32 truncated to 0 and
threw a TypeError during ReadableStream construction, while 2^32 + 1
truncated to 1 byte instead of rejecting read requests with RangeError.

[iOS] Add unit tests for closing Manage Accounts navigation controller

In https://crbug.com/429973108, tearing down or closing an accounts
`SettingsNavigationController` caused infinite recursion until stack
overflow: `-[SettingsNavigationController cleanUpSettings]` called
`-[ManageAccountsCoordinator stop]`, which called `-closeViewController`
and `-popViewControllerOrCloseSettingsAnimated:`, invoking
`-[SettingsNavigationController closeSettings]` and re-entering
`-cleanUpSettings` through the delegate. https://crrev.com/c/6714866
resolved that production crash by making `SettingsNavigationController`
always own `ManageAccountsCoordinator` and having
`-[ManageAccountsCoordinator stop]` only pop its view controller without
closing settings.

Add `CleanUpAccountsControllerDoesNotCloseSettings` and
`CloseAccountsControllerFromDoneButtonWithoutRecursion` in
`SettingsNavigationControllerTest` to verify that `-cleanUpSettings`
does not notify the delegate to close settings and that closing from the
Done button notifies the delegate once without recursing.

[iOS] Format the blocked popup count for the current locale

The blocked popups infobar message (`IDS_IOS_POPUPS_BLOCKED_MOBILE`)
received the number of blocked popups formatted with
`base::StringPrintf("%" PRIuS)`, which always uses ASCII digits and no
grouping separators. Locales that use other digits (e.g. Arabic,
Persian, Bengali) displayed Latin digits in the middle of localized
text.

This CL uses `base::FormatNumber()` instead, and adds the `//base:i18n`
dependency it requires. The output is unchanged for English (the count
is a small integer), so `window_open_by_dom_egtest.mm`, which expects
"1", still passes.

This CL adds
`BlockedPopupTabHelperTest.MessageTextFormattedAcrossLocales`, which
verifies the whole message in English, French, German, Japanese, and
Arabic (`ar-EG`): `ui::test::ScopedApplicationLocale` loads the
translation of `IDS_IOS_POPUPS_BLOCKED_MOBILE` for the locale, and the
count, greater than 1000, is formatted with the grouping separator and
digits of the locale. The expected strings are the current translations
from the `.xtb` files.

Steps to reproduce:
1. In the iOS Settings app, set the language of Chrome to Arabic.
2. Open a page that calls `window.open()` on load without a user
   gesture.
Before: The blocked pop-ups infobar ("Pop-ups blocked (1)" in English)
shows the count as the Latin digit "1" in the Arabic text.
After: The count is shown as the Arabic-Indic digit "١".

quic: Abort AsyncDnsJob on network change or disconnect errors

When a connection attempt in QuicSessionPool::AsyncDnsJob fails with
ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED or ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED, the endpoints held by
the job belong to the prior network state (or no network is available).
Continuing to try remaining candidates can connect using stale DNS
answers or overwrite the error with a later failure, which can falsely
mark the alternative service broken.

Stop advancing EndpointConnector and complete AsyncDnsJob immediately
with the error when an attempt fails synchronously or asynchronously
with ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED or ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED, canceling any
other in-flight connector. Do the same when the resolver finishes with
one of these errors after a fresh attempt has started, instead of
ignoring the resolver error. Gate this behavior behind a
default-enabled feature parameter kAsyncDnsQuicJobAbortOnNetworkChange
on kAsyncDnsQuicJob so it can be toggled independently if needed (e.g.
for network transition handoffs where remaining endpoints stay valid).

Keep the two OnNetworkDisconnected fallback/pooling tests from
crrev.com/c/8817489 running with the parameter disabled, in addition to
new tests covering immediate job failure when enabled.

[Theme] Drop NewTabPageCustomizationV2 param show_logo_and_search_box

NewTabPageCustomizationV2 is enabled by default and about to be removed.
Its show_logo_and_search_box param defaults to true, which is the
launched behavior, so it only adds a dead branch to the upload image
preview.

In this CL:
- Delete the show_logo_and_search_box param; the upload image preview
  always shows the logo and the search box.
- Drop the param from the new-tab-page-customization-v2 chrome://flags
  variations.

Original change's description:
> [speech] Call SodaPreSandboxInit before engaging Linux speech sandbox
>
> Follow-up to crrev.com/c/8830057. Instead of unconditionally brokering
> /proc/cpuinfo inside the Linux speech recognition sandbox for XNNPACK
> cpuinfo initialization, resolve and invoke the optional
> SodaPreSandboxInit export from libsoda.so before StartBrokerProcess().
>
> When SodaPreSandboxInit is present and succeeds, omit /proc/cpuinfo from
> the broker allowlist immediately. For older SODA binaries that do not
> export SodaPreSandboxInit (or if initialization returns false), keep
> read-only /proc/cpuinfo access as a temporary fallback so Linux XNNPACK
> delegation does not regress during SODA rollout.
>

[chromecast] Record Android MediaCodec release interval UMA

When MediaCodec renders directly to an Android SurfaceView overlay
(DialogOverlayImpl), releaseOutputBuffer(index, true) bypasses Android
API 21+ renderTimestampNs and queues buffers to SurfaceFlinger with
timestamp=0 (immediate latch). If two output buffers are released
within a single display VSync (< 8 ms apart on a 60 Hz display),
SurfaceFlinger overwrites the pending buffer in the BufferQueue slot
before VSync latches it, causing a silent frame drop that is invisible
to Viz and Blink frame counters.

Record three UMA histograms in CodecWrapperImpl:

- Media.CodecWrapper.IsOverlayBacked (once per configured surface on
  its first rendered output buffer)
- Media.CodecOutputBuffer.ReleaseInterval.{Overlay,TextureOwner}
- Media.CodecOutputBuffer.SubVsyncRelease.{Overlay,TextureOwner}

Bug: b:560033352
Test: media_unittests --gtest_filter=CodecWrapperTest.*

[A11y] Deflake AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName dump test

DumpAccessibilityTreeTest.AccessibilityNoSourceVideoAuthorName/linux
failed 1 of 20 repeats in the new-test flakiness check on
linux_chromium_asan_rel_ng. In the failing run the dumped tree was
missing one of the whitespace static text nodes between the inline
<video> elements; every other line matched the expectation.

The test covers the accessible names of the media elements, not the
whitespace between them. Make the elements in the test page
block-level so that the whitespace between them generates no nodes,
and drop those nodes from the expectation files.

[webui] Turn off V8 builtins PGO in cros:v8_snapshot

This CL turns off V8 builtins PGO in `cros:v8_snapshot`, matching the
ChromeOS target.

Without this CL, ChromeOS uprevs fail to build. Since
https://crrev.com/c/8835602, this toolchain builds a V8 snapshot for
`code_cache_generator`. Its `current_os = "linux"` turns on builtins PGO
for official builds, so `mksnapshot` needs
`v8/tools/builtins-pgo/profiles/x64.profile`, which the ChromeOS ebuild
never downloads.

With PGO off, the generator's builtins also match the target's
`snapshot_blob.bin`, which the generator loads.

Fix URL bar blank in Full WebUI Omnibox

The omnibox doesn't show zerosuggestions when on about:blank[0].

An initial navigation to about:blank auto-focuses the omnibox[1].

The actor framework (agent using Chrome), as one example, creates new
tabs to about:blank[2] before navigating them to another URL. However,
after navigating to the subsequent URL the omnibox continues to display
"about:blank" (that's the bug).

This happens because OmniboxEditModel::ResetDisplayTexts prevents
navigations from replacing the current omnibox text if the suggestions
are showing [3]. However, that uses IsPopupOpen to determine if
suggestions are shown which always returns true if
kWebUIOmniboxFullPopup is enabled, even when the suggestions aren't
showing because of [0] (I'm guessing because the searchbar itself is now
WebUI and considered part of the popup)?

This CL updates OmniboxEditModel::ResetDisplayTexts to explicitly look
at whether suggestions are showing. This also requires synchronizing the
native view with the WebUI popup whenever the shown text is reverted.

91b7ed1118423f4dbd01bb77ce58de1c0512b300 [ diff ] 
[DeclarativePerformanceObserver] Skip saturated TimeDelta entries

`performance.mark(name, {startTime})` accepts any non-negative finite
`DOMHighResTimeStamp`. Converting timestamps in the renderer via
`base::Milliseconds()` saturates values above `int64_t` max
microseconds (~9.22e15 ms) to `base::TimeDelta::Max()`. Because Mojo's
`TimeDelta` traits perform no range validation, calling
`InMillisecondsF()` on a saturated `TimeDelta` produces `+/-inf` and
hits `DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED()` in `base::Value::DoubleStorage`.

Keep `mojo_base.mojom.TimeDelta` on the Mojo interface per IPC time
type guidelines, and skip `DeclarativePerformanceMark` and
`DeclarativeLargestContentfulPaint` entries with `is_inf()` timestamps
in `DeclarativePerformanceObserver::DidObservePerformanceEntries()`.
Skipping rather than calling `mojo::ReportBadMessage` avoids
terminating valid renderers when web content passes a large finite
`startTime`.

[crubit] Include variant*.rs in cc_std for ToT Crubit

Tip-of-tree Crubit added `pub use cc_std::{trivial_variant, variant};`
to `support/cpp_std.rs` along with four new `variant*.rs` files under
`support/cc_std_impl/`. Because `//build/rust/crubit:cc_std` lists
`extra_rust_source_groups` manually, ToT Rust builds failed compiling
`//build/rust/crubit:cpp_std` with unresolved imports.

Include `variant.rs`, `variant_coproduct.rs`, `variant_enums.rs`, and
`variant_internal.rs` in `cc_std`'s `std` module when
`rust_force_head_revision` is true, so ToT builds pass now while pinned
toolchains (which do not yet contain these files) continue to build.

[Reading mode PDFs] Record table count and shape metrics

Add metrics to see how often grid table detection finds tables and
what they look like, to help tune the detector:

- Accessibility.PdfHeuristics.TableCountPerPage: once per untagged
  page with text, including pages with no tables.
- TableRowCount, TableColumnCount, TablePopulatedCellPercentage, and
  TableMaxCellLength: once per detected table.

A high max cell length suggests a paragraph was pulled into a cell.

Only recorded when kPdfAccessibilityHeuristicEnhancements is enabled.

ee2766abc4e3094d5680e27e5d03b10f1e534b69 [ diff ] 
[blink] Pass animated colors from ComputedStyle to cc::PaintFlags

Adds AnimatedColor, which pairs a resolved Color with the AnimatedSource
that drives it, so raster can update the color without a main-thread
repaint.

Behind CompositeColorAnimation, starting with box backgrounds:

- ComputedStyle::VisitedDependentAnimatedColor() returns an
  AnimatedColor for a color property.
- AnimatedColor::ToPaintColor() converts it to a cc::PaintColor, setting
  needs_main_thread_repaint when the source has untracked dependencies.
- Box background painters pass that cc::PaintColor through
  GraphicsContext into cc::PaintFlags.
- ComputedStyle::HasBackground() returns true when background-color has
  an AnimatedSource, so a transparent background still paints.

CompositeColorAnimation is disabled by default, so there is no behavior
change.

Ash: Migrate AmbientPhotoControllerTest off RunUntilIdle

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to modernize Ash tests by
migrating them away from RunUntilIdle() and toward targeted
synchronization with APIs such as RunUntil(), TestFuture, RunLoop
callbacks, observer waiters, or exact mock-time advancement.

ShouldResumeWhenHaveMoreTopics now waits for the second image after
FetchTopics(), using the fixture's RunUntilNextTopicsAdded(), because
the check reads the model's next image, which is the second one added.
Each image is added only after the posted photo download reply and the
decode run. RunUntil() won't do here: under MOCK_TIME, once no task is
ready it fast-forwards to the next delayed one, such as the topic
queue's 30 second refetch timer, before it checks the predicate. Three
calls stay, because nothing tells the test that the work they wait for
is done. The first one in ShouldResumeWhenHaveMoreTopics waits for the
chain of empty cache reads that FetchImage() starts, which ends in a
single image failure that notifies no observer. The ones in
ShouldStartDownloadBackupImagesOnAmbientModeStart and
UsesBackupCacheAfterPrimaryCacheCleared wait for the backup photo
downloads, which report completion only to AmbientPhotoController's
private OnBackupImageFetched().

[SidePanel] Plumb header icon to Android

Pass the side panel entry's header icon to the Android side panel
header.
-Previously, the header's icon could only be set from Java, and no side
 panel entry could provide it.
-Now, SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid passes the entry's kSidePanelIconKey
 image to Java as a Bitmap, the same way Android extension action icons
 are passed. Only bitmap icons are supported for now.

> PaintTiming: Add LargestContentfulPaintCalculator::PendingMetricsData
>
> This is another step towards creating LCP/ICP entries and metrics data
> at paint time. This CL adds PendingMetricsData, which encapsulates the
> data needed at presentation time. In this CL, we compute this data at
> presentation time, but we'll eventually compute it at paint time and
> propagate to presentation time (via Delegates). Splitting this out will
> isolate behavioral changes in a future patch, as this is a essentially a
> pure refactor**.
>
> **This also fixes a long-standing edge case where in the event of a
> tie between image and text size for the per-frame largest candidate,
> we would use the text, but everywhere else (i.e. metrics) uses the
> image.

[SideUi] Ignore trailing touch events after interrupting a drag (3/6)

Ignore trailing touch events when an in-progress resize drag is
interrupted externally.
-Previously, pausing Side UI updates or destroying the handle mid-drag
 cleared drag state immediately, so remaining events from that gesture
 would record unexpected *_WITHOUT_DRAG histogram samples.
-Now, SideUiResizeHandler#interruptDrag marks the gesture interrupted so
 remaining move/up/cancel events are ignored until the next ACTION_DOWN.

Treat Ask Google privacy notice acknowledgement as onboarding

Ask Google entry points display the Ask Google privacy notice instead of
the standard onboarding tooltip, which leaves the post-onboarding
session count uninitialized. This change treats dismissing that notice
as onboarding so the session count can increment and users can become
eligible for the pinning promo.

[History Clusters] Remove HistoryClustersOnDeviceClustering feature

`kOnDeviceClustering` has been `ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT` since it was
introduced, and owners confirmed it is safe to remove.

The feature was only used to read Finch params in `Config::Config()`.
With it removed, Config's in-class defaults are used directly.

Note: Config::content_visibility_threshold's in-class default is changed
from 0.7 to 0.5 to preserve current behavior. Since crrev.com/c/4378099
(2023), the constructor always overrode it with a Finch fallback of 0.5,
so 0.7 was never the effective value.

[VideoStack] Fix HEVC clip filename and continue past clip errors

The 1080p60 HEVC clip in the videostack_videos_30s CIPD package is
named 1080p60fpsHEVC_boat_sync.mp4, without "_yt_". Requesting
1080p60fpsHEVC_boat_yt_sync.mp4 returned HTTP 404 from the local server,
spent 65 seconds recording a blank screen, and aborted the suite before
1080p60fpsVP9_boat_yt_sync.webm could run.

Point common.VIDEOS at 1080p60fpsHEVC_boat_sync.mp4, fail immediately
when a reference video is missing on the host, and continue running
remaining clips after a per-clip error before re-raising.

[a11y] Swap or copy children instead of guarding child loops

This CL simplifies GuardedChildren (crrev.com/c/8670121) to swap when
clearing and copy when walking, as suggested in review
(crrev.com/c/8710172).

GuardedChildren sets a bool while a loop walks children_ so nested
clears and rebuilds return early. This CL removes the guard and swaps or
copies instead:
- ClearChildren() swaps children_ into a local vector and never calls
  clear(). Nested clears and rebuilds see an empty children_ and use a
  new buffer. The GC keeps the local vector alive during the loop and
  frees it after.
- RemoveIncludedSubtree() walks a local copy.
- RemoveSubtreeInternal() removes inline text boxes without a copy. They
  are leaves, so removing one cannot create re-entrancy.
- RemoveSubtreeInternal() copies only children still parented by object.

Copying only when needed avoids the Pinpoint regression from an earlier
swap and copy attempt.

Skipping clear() doesn't move the same work into a later GC. The GC
already sweeps every page, and it frees a dead buffer for less work than
clear() does.

Pinpoint shows no overall change on Speedometer 3 or
blink_perf.accessibility on Linux, Windows, Mac, and Android.

This CL also updates a stale comment in RemoveSubtreeInternal(). It said
inline text boxes share their parent's node, but AXInlineTextBox no
longer overrides GetNode() (GetNode() CL: crrev.com/c/5783365).

SECURITY_PRESUBMIT_BYPASS_REASON=This CL is an alternate way to do a recent fix (crrev.com/c/8670121) that does not introduce a security regression and also fixes the attached bug. The longer-term fix is tracked in go/ax-owns-projection-prototype.

[Task Manager] Use `IcuBridge::ListFormatter::FormatStandardList()`

`TaskManagerTableModel::FormatListToString()`, used to build the
accessible names of the Task Manager rows and table header, contained a
private copy of the ICU `ListFormatter` boilerplate. Replace it with
`base::i18n::IcuBridge::ListFormatter::FormatStandardList()` via
`base::i18n::IcuBridge::GetInstance().list_formatter()`.

This is a refactor with no behavior change: both create the ICU
`ListFormatter` for the default locale with the standard conjunction
pattern (`ULISTFMT_TYPE_AND`, `ULISTFMT_WIDTH_WIDE`), so the output is
unchanged in every locale, e.g. "a, b, and c" in English or "a, b et c"
in French. The only difference is the ICU-failure path, which used to
`CHECK()` and now joins the items with ", ".

The ICU dependencies of `//chrome/browser/ui/task_manager:task_manager`
are removed, since no file in that target uses ICU directly anymore.

The new `TaskManagerTableModelTest.FormatListToStringAcrossLocales`
pins the output in `en-US`, `fr`, `zh-CN` and the right-to-left `ar`,
switching the locale with `ui::test::ScopedApplicationLocale`.

No screenshot: the change only affects accessible names of the Task
Manager table, and the native accessibility tree of non-browser windows
can't be shown in `chrome://accessibility` on Linux.

Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter=TaskManagerTableModelTest.*

webui: Inject MetricsService into PerSessionSettingsUserActionTracker

Inject a MetricsServiceGetter callback
(base::RepeatingCallback<metrics::MetricsService*()>) into
PerSessionSettingsUserActionTracker instead of reading
g_browser_process->metrics_service() in HasUserMetricsConsent(). This
removes the last g_browser_process use in
chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash/settings/services/metrics, so drop
//chrome/browser:browser_process from BUILD.gn and
+chrome/browser/browser_process.h from DEPS.

Dependency flow:
  OsSettingsManagerFactory::BuildServiceInstanceForBrowserContext()
    -> OsSettingsManager
      -> SettingsUserActionTracker
        -> PerSessionSettingsUserActionTracker

MetricsService is destroyed in BrowserProcessImpl::StartTearDown(),
before ProfileManager destroys profiles and their KeyedServices
(including OsSettingsManager). Storing a raw_ptr or raw_ref on
OsSettingsManager or SettingsUserActionTracker would dangle during
shutdown, so pass a getter callback for now (crbug.com/558489113).

HasUserMetricsConsent() CHECKs that the returned MetricsService is
non-null: BrowserProcessImpl::metrics_service() is non-null from
BrowserProcessImpl construction (https://crrev.com/c/8378621) until
StartTearDown(), and HasUserMetricsConsent() is only called via WebUI
Mojo IPC while OSSettingsUI is alive inside the main RunLoop.

[WebView] Fix header-name comparator in GetCombinedMatchingHeaders

`HeaderNameComparator::operator()` in
`AwOriginMatchedHeader::GetCombinedMatchingHeaders` returned the `int`
result of `base::CompareCaseInsensitiveASCII` (-1, 0, or 1) directly to
`base::flat_map`. Because `base::flat_map` uses its comparator as a
strict weak ordering (`<`) predicate, both -1 and 1 converted to `true`
("not equal" rather than "less than").

When multiple distinct header names were present, `find()` missed
existing entries, differently capitalized duplicates were returned as
separate entries instead of being comma-joined, and the backing vector
was left unsorted. Fix the comparator to return `bool` using `< 0`, and
add a multi-header regression test.

Bug: 588060977
Test: android_webview_unittests --gtest_filter=AwOriginMatchedHeaderTest.*

[ARC] Localize the key list of input overlay accessible labels

The accessible label of an input overlay control lists its keys, e.g.
"w, a, s, d" for a joystick. The keys were joined with a hardcoded Latin
comma (`u", "`), which is wrong in locales that use another separator,
e.g. "w、a、s、d" in Japanese.

Use `base::i18n::IcuBridge::ListFormatter::FormatNarrowList()` via
`base::i18n::IcuBridge::GetInstance().list_formatter()` in
`EditLabels::CalculateKeyListForA11yLabel()`. Since the localized list
may not contain a ",", `ActionEditView::CalculateAccessibleLabel()` can
no longer detect a multi-key control by searching for ","; it now uses
the new `EditLabels::GetKeyCount()` instead. The English output is
unchanged.

`EditLabelTest.KeyListForA11yLabelAcrossLocales` in `unit_tests`
verifies the key count and the accessible key list in `en-US`, `fr`,
`de`, `ja`, and `ar`, switching locale with
`ui::test::ScopedApplicationLocale`.

Steps to reproduce:
1. On ChromeOS, set the device language to Japanese and turn on
   ChromeVox.
2. Open an Android game that supports game controls, then open the Game
   Dashboard.
3. In the "Controls" row, click "Set up" (or "Edit game controls"), and
   create a joystick control with the keys w, a, s and d.
4. Move the ChromeVox focus to the joystick in the controls list.
Before: ChromeVox reads the keys separated by ", ".
After: ChromeVox reads the keys as "w、a、s、d".

Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter=EditLabelTest.*:ActionViewTest.*

[Android][voice_search] Siphon foreground audio into webkit

Android's SpeechRecognizer (speech webkit) opens the microphone inside
the separate recognition service process, which Android classifies as
background and because it is background, it is silenced when another
foreground stream records concurrently. This is because 2 audio streams
are not allowed due to CPU/power-drain, HAL hardware mode-switching
limitations, and privacy issues (spyware) in android devices.

Because Chrome cannot promote another app's process into Android's
foreground mic list, attach microphone stream to capture from Chrome's
existing foreground process (making speech webkit "like" a foreground
process, without the forced quit audio due to lack of priority) on
version Android Tiramisu+ (behind a default-enabled Finch killswitch
AndroidSpeechRecognitionInProcessAudio):

- Open AudioRecord (VOICE_RECOGNITION, 16kHz, mono, PCM_16BIT) inside
  Chrome's foreground process on a dedicated audio thread and stream raw
  audio bytes over a ParcelFileDescriptor pipe via EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE.
  This allows speech recognition to effectively be a foreground audio
  process without literally being a foreground process. The recognizer
  starts once AudioRecord opens, falling back to SpeechRecognizer's
  default capture if setup fails.
- Stop and release AudioRecord on the audio thread that reads it, and
  close the pipe across all session exit paths (end of speech, stop,
  abort, error, and native destroy) so the OS mic indicator releases
  promptly.
- For single-utterance sessions, request a segmented session keyed off a
  5s EXTRA_SPEECH_INPUT_COMPLETE_SILENCE_LENGTH_MILLIS and complete on
  onSegmentResults(). Otherwise EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE disables the
  recognizer's default 5s silence timeout and delivers the final result
  via onPartialResults(), leaving voice search waiting.
- Map ERROR_RECOGNIZER_BUSY to AUDIO_CAPTURE and terminate unknown
  SpeechRecognizer error codes with ABORTED instead of asserting.

With EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE, the recognition service does not take transient
audio focus, so media keeps playing during recognition, matching
desktop.

screencast/cast/NDU2Njk3NjYxNjcyNjUyOHw3NWZkMjJkMC1iNw

[Keyboard Shortcuts] Disable top-chrome shortcuts in fullscreen

In fullscreen mode, top browser controls (toolbar, omnibox, tab strip,
and bookmark bar) are hidden, so shortcuts like Alt+F open a disembodied
3-dot app menu or shift focus onto invisible UI.

Gate app-menu, focus, bookmark-bar, feedback, and tab-strip contextual
commands on !isFullscreen() in BrowserCommandDelegate, matching
Desktop's BrowserCommandController::UpdateCommandsForFullscreenMode()
while keeping tab, find, and page shortcuts enabled.

NO_IFTTT=Updating BrowserCommandDelegate enablement only; legacy KeyboardShortcuts is frozen behind AndroidUnifiedKeyboardShortcuts.

[composebox] Stop selecting text on paste action

Previously, `QueryActionOverride.kPaste` highlighted the entire
prefilled prompt after focusing the Composebox input, causing subsequent
typing to overwrite the suggested prompt instead of appending to it.
Keep focusing the input on paste actions while leaving the caret
collapsed at the end of the text, and remove the now-unused
`selectAll()` helper.

Screencast of the paste behavior after fix (After the prompt is pasted,
the user can use tab key to focus voice search button, which meets the
a11y requirement):

3330a602fe8a8956a20ecb31b2e8ef004fc689d7 [ diff ] 
Scale link drag image border inset by device scale factor

DragRectForLink() places the cursor kLinkDragBorderInset pixels below
the top edge of the link drag image. The image is drawn in DIPs on a
canvas scaled by the device scale factor, including its label padding,
but the inset was applied in physical pixels. With a device scale factor
of 2, the cursor therefore ended up 1 DIP below the top edge instead of
2.

Scale the inset by the device scale factor and round it up to whole
pixels, as WebFrameWidgetImpl::StartDragging() floors the cursor offset
to DIPs. With a device scale factor of 1.2, the 2.4 pixel inset would
otherwise become 2 pixels once the drag rect is rounded to whole pixels,
which is floored to 1 DIP, while 3 pixels gives 2 DIPs.

With a page scale factor other than 1, the cursor can still end up 1
DIP short, as DoSystemDrag() maps the drag rect to the viewport in whole
pixels (crbug.com/331753420). This is left for a separate change.

Also replace kLinkDragBorderInset with kDragLabelBorderY, now in
drag_image.h, so the inset and the label padding share one constant, and
correct the comment about DoSystemDrag(), which maps the origin of the
drag rect but not its size to the viewport.

This is a follow-up to https://crrev.com/c/8814720, suggested in its
review.

[iOS] Support Account Switching promo in fullscreen sign-in screen

This CL ensures that the `FullscreenSigninScreen` coordinators and
mediators can display the account switch promo, record metric, observe
accounts on device and dismisses itself if needed.
